# Accessibility development instructions

Use these instructions when creating or remediating web content or non-web documents. Apply [the starter instructions](accessibility-starter.md) and the appropriate development/creation skill as task guidance, either directly or through a supported tool. Consult the bundled scope reference and retrieve the criterion entries, applicable Baseline procedures, and document-format guidance relevant to the task. Use the complete reference materials to identify applicable requirements when necessary, but avoid unnecessarily loading entire reference documents into the agent's working context.

For web work, use [accessible-web-development](../../../.agents/skills/accessible-web-development/SKILL.md). Document-format resources are not bundled; obtain them separately when needed.

1. Establish all applicable WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A/AA criteria and the relevant Baseline procedures. Use the bundled criterion and procedure inventories to retain missing-case and review gaps. Record non-web exceptions, no-test-required dispositions and supplemental checks distinctly.
2. Build a task-oriented artifact with native structure: headings/lists/tables, meaningful names and alternatives, reading/focus order, input labels/errors, usable controls and accessible media. Preserve intent and data semantics. Draft text alternatives from the image's purpose and context, distinguish decoration, and obtain human review; do not invent missing meaning or values.
3. Apply newer contrast, responsive presentation, hover/focus, pointer, input, help and authentication guidance where applicable; label it supplemental rather than mapped to a Baseline. Use the exact criterion exceptions and format-appropriate interpretation.
4. Save an initial artifact and inspect the actual rendered/native delivery. Combine supported automated checks with human keyboard, visual comparison and applicable assistive technology. Do not fabricate capability-dependent checks.
5. Make the smallest effective remediation in a working copy, preserving formulas, links, text, interactions and security/redactions. Retest affected requirements and likely regressions in the same environment; record initial/final stages separately. Identify and correct newly introduced accessibility failures, even if the overall number of reported defects decreases.
6. Verify exports and dependencies independently. Report actual outcomes, unresolved issues, coverage limitations and human-review status. Do not claim completed validation because every instruction or catalog entry exists.
